proposal: Raise the football fetcher's maxEvents cap from 30 to 90 so the static pipeline stops silently dropping whole COVERED leagues. Once improve PR #466 added Serie A (ita.1) + Bundesliga (ger.1) as wholesale ESPN leagues, every normal matchweek the seven configured leagues (PL/La Liga/Serie A/Bundesliga/CL/Eliteserien/OBOS) over a 7-day window exceed 30: measured 42 events on a non-CL week and 66 on a Champions League week. The 30-cut drops the tail — today's football.json is Eliteserien(7)+PL(9)+La Liga(9)+Serie A(5)=exactly 30, with Bundesliga(9) and part of Serie A gone even though ESPN ger.1 returns the fixtures. build-events' graft-then-drop then makes hand-boarded ai-research CL/Bundesliga events disappear for good when the window next cuts them — the recurring Sep MD1 regression. Fix is a threshold tune (the research agent's own prescribed cure: 'hev/segmenter maxEvents'); football is catalog tier1 so the cap is a swamp guard only, sized to hold the heaviest realistic week. Also updated the fetcher's explanatory comment and made tests/football-fetcher.test.js derive the cap from config so the domestic-first ordering guarantee can't be silently un-tested by a future cap change.
evidence: Reproduced live: the football fetcher gets 42 pre-filter events {PL:9, La Liga:9, Serie A:8, Bundesliga:9, Eliteserien:7} but the maxEvents:30 cut yields {Eliteserien:7, PL:9, La Liga:9, Serie A:5} — Bundesliga dropped entirely, Serie A truncated 8→5. docs/data/football.json currently holds exactly those 30 and no Bundesliga.

ESPN ger.1 is NOT broken (research-log 2026-10-05 hypothesised 'ger.1-endepunktet ser tomt/ødelagt ut'): a direct query returns Bundesliga Spieltag fixtures for 9–11 Oct (Dortmund–Werder, 6 Sat matches, 2 Sun) and for 17/24/31 Oct — 6+ events per matchday. The cap, not the endpoint, is eating them.

tracked.json champions-league-2026-27 carries the same root-cause flag run-after-run: 2026-09-06 'Den EKTE årsaken ... er maxEvents:30-kuttet ... FLAGG (self-repair/improve): hev/segmenter maxEvents', 2026-09-07 'ROTÅRSAK STÅR ... Varig kur: hev/segmenter maxEvents per liga', 2026-09-08 'ROTÅRSAK UENDRET ... (nå tredje kjøring på rad)'. The cut + build-events graft-then-drop caused repeated CL MD1 regressions where boarded fixtures vanished on the next window.

improve PR #466 (2026-09-28) added ita.1 + ger.1 to the fetcher but explicitly left maxEvents unchanged ('no maxEvents change') on the belief the Norwegian-first ordering protected coverage — it protects domestic/marquee, not whole non-Norwegian leagues, so Bundesliga (least Norwegian-relevant, ordered last) falls past the 30-cut.

Heaviest realistic week measured at 66 (CL matchday week: PL 10, La Liga 11, Serie A 10, Bundesliga 9, CL 18, Eliteserien 8); 90 gives headroom without being a target — typical weeks render ~42 and the cap effectively never bites.
npm test: 88 files / 1541 tests pass, incl. the updated tests/football-fetcher.test.js (cap derived from sportsConfig; still proves Eliteserien stays ahead of foreign leagues when the cap bites).
expectedEffect: Bundesliga + full Serie A rounds land on the board from the static pipeline (free, hourly) every matchweek instead of being hand-boarded as source:ai-research. Champions League matchdays beyond day 1 stop being cut and stop regressing out after build-events grafts the static fixture, ending the run-after-run MD re-boarding the research agent has done since early September. Fewer research passes spent re-boarding mechanically-available fixtures.
howWeKnow: football.json contains Bundesliga (ger.1) fixtures on a matchweek; Serie A is not truncated; coverage-audit stops emitting the Serie A/Bundesliga research-dependence sourceIssue; tracked.json champions-league stops logging the maxEvents:30 root-cause flag + the MD regression; CL matchdays board as source:espn and do not disappear between runs.
notes: Smallest change that delivers the flagged durable cure: one threshold (30→90) + its explanatory comment + a cap-derived test. No per-league segmentation machinery (the research agent's 'hev/segmenter' — the simpler 'hev' suffices because football is wholesale-covered, so every fixture the fetcher produces is in-scope and the cap serves only as a swamp guard).
iOS live-league parity (LiveLeague.forEvent) unaffected — this is a fetcher count cap, not a league set; the separate ios track is untouched.
